approvals.title: Approval chain
approvals.sub: {{n}} tenders above the operator's own authority — each with the body its decision waits on, and where that decision stands.
approvals.explainTitle: What is this chain? — the approval ladder at its current ceilings
approvals.explainIntro: Every purchase request is measured by its estimated value against an approval ladder: a system default that applies to every operating company, unless the platform administrator has approved a ladder for one company in particular, in which case that company alone is measured against it. The ladder — not the kind of work — is what decides who signs, and only tenders that passed their own company's authority appear here.
approvals.explainFailClosed: Both ceilings are inclusive: a value equal to the ceiling stays in the lower tier. If the ladder configuration is missing or out of order, the tender is read conservatively as the highest tier — a request whose clearing body cannot be established must not be treated as cleared by the lowest one.
approvals.localLadder: The ladder ceilings are in-app configuration, and so are the per-operator ladders: no server route issues them yet; the figures shown are the same ones the tiers are derived from here.

approvals.waitDef: Working days elapsed since the ratification stage's planned end (weekends and official holidays excluded) — not a calendar count, and not an unsupported alarm threshold.
approvals.waitOnPlan: Within the ratification stage's planned window — its date has not passed yet.
approvals.waitUnplanned: The ratification stage carries no planned end date, so its lateness cannot be measured — a «0» here would read as «on time».

match.def: «Plan conformance» compares what was actually done with what was planned: for each stage the difference between its planned and its actual completion date is counted in working days (weekends and public holidays excluded); positive is late, negative is early — and the tender's status follows where today sits against the end of its current stage.
match.devDef: The difference in working days between a stage's planned and actual completion — and, for the stage still open, between its planned end and today. Positive is late, negative is early.

reports.title: Reports
reports.hint: Every figure is recomputed from state via the engine — nothing is stored.
reports.briefDesc: An official A4 page on your own report template: the approval ladder with its live ceilings and queues, your portfolio today, and what changed in the platform — to read on screen or print.
reports.scopePortfolio: The whole portfolio — no date window
reports.vendorTitle: Vendor report — specialization and financial capacity
reports.vendorCaveat: Derived from the scopes it has competed in — pending the official classification. The store holds no specialization field, so the classification below is an inference from the participation and award record, not a list issued by the ministry.
reports.vendorExplainScope: Specialization: how many tenders the entity actually bid on, spread across the four §9 work scopes. «Primary scope» is the most frequent one; a tie prints «undetermined» rather than inventing a preference.
reports.vendorExplainBands: The financial-capacity bands ARE the SYSTEM DEFAULT approval ladder ({{op}} operator authority · {{jmc}} joint-committee ceiling) applied to the total value of contracts awarded to the entity. They stay on the default deliberately even where operators hold custom ladders: an entity's won value is aggregated across several operators, so there is no single operator whose ladder could be resolved for it. A governed ladder was chosen over statistical quantiles because a quantile band moves when the data moves: an entity slides from one band to another without any fact about it changing.
reports.vendorExplainName: An entity is bound to its contracts by vendor id where one exists, otherwise by contractor name (the same 12.4.2 rule that binds a bidder to its registry entry). A contract carrying neither is attributed to nobody.
reports.vendorEmpty: No entities registered yet — no participation or awards to derive a classification from.

sched.sub: Planned against actual — every tender on its current stage, every contract on its progress

sched.explainTitle: What exactly does this table measure?
sched.explainTender: A tender row measures its current stage only: planned date against actual, and the gap in WORKING days (not calendar days) under the recorded public-holiday calendar. Positive is late, negative is ahead.
sched.explainContract: A contract row measures a different unit: the share of stages closed against the share whose planned date has passed — a gap in percentage POINTS, not in days. The two units are never added together.
sched.explainAllTime: The «Schedule adherence — since inception» tile is the figure shown in the follow-up room, from the same derivation: a ratio over EVERY closed stage that carried a plan, across the whole portfolio, unaffected by the filters on this screen. The four tiles beside it count the FILTERED rows of the table below, each request on its current stage only. Two different windows; neither is subtracted from the other.
sched.explainStatusScope: The «status» filter applies to tenders alone: its vocabulary (at risk / late / complete / in progress) is tender-status vocabulary, and neither the contracts table nor its stamp reads it — a contract's verdict is measured in percentage points, not in those words.
sched.explainUnplanned: A stage with no planned date cannot be judged: it reads «unplanned» and is excluded from the average deviation — «no plan» is not «no deviation».
sched.explainCompleted: A completed tender has no current stage, so its row reads the last stage it actually closed, and says so.
sched.explainNotSection9: This screen is about time alone. «Compliance & committees» is a different screen answering local content (§9 / Article 25) and committee nominations (12.2).
sched.kpiAllTimeHint: The same figure as the follow-up room — unaffected by this screen's filters
sched.tenderTable: Tenders — current stage against its plan
sched.contractNote: The gap here is in percentage points between closed stages and stages already due; a contract is attributed to a company through its originating tender, so a contract without one is unaffected by the company filter.
sched.contractStatusNote: The status filter applies to tenders — neither this table nor its stamp reads it, so the contract rows below have not been narrowed by it.
sched.noStages: No stages recorded for this tender

fact.archive: Archiving instead of deletion: no record is erased — it is archived and stays readable in the registry and the audit trail.
fact.stamp: Every printout and every CSV leaves stamped with the active filters, the row count and the issue date.
fact.schedule: The schedule-compliance screen: planned against actual for every stage and every contract, in working days.
fact.merged: Registering an operating company and its fields is now one wizard instead of two separate screens.
fact.gate: The role gate: the admin panel is closed to company-scoped roles, and every decision fails closed unless the actor's authority is established.
fact.access: One access section holds accounts, roles and permissions — including the Joint Management Committee (JMC) seat.

opladder.title: This company's approval ladder
opladder.currentDefault: This company is on the system default.
opladder.currentOwn: This company is on a custom approved ladder.
opladder.errNumber: Both ceilings must be finite figures, neither below zero.
opladder.errOrder: The company ceiling must be STRICTLY below the committee ceiling: equal ceilings describe an empty T2 band, which is an ambiguity rather than a two-tier ladder.
opladder.errNoChange: No change from the ladder in force — and no row is written for a change that did not happen.
opladder.zeroNote: A zero company ceiling is deliberately allowed: it sends every one of the company's requests above its own tier.
opladder.previewNone: No pending tender of this company changes tier under this ladder.
opladder.previewLive: The preview is derived right now from this company's live, undecided tenders, and they are measured by the new ladder the moment it is approved: the tier is read at decision time and never stored.
opladder.resetNote: Withdrawing a custom ladder is a full governed act with its own justification and actor, not a silent erase; the company returns to the system default immediately.
opladder.apiBlocked: Editing per-operator ladders is withheld in server mode: there is no model for custom ladders and no endpoint yet, and the server rules by the default ladder alone. Approving a ceiling the server does not enforce would make the disabled button and the 403 refusal disagree, so the editor stays closed until the route lands.
